title: feat: pause the Bee Census and add the Honey Census for Pollen buyers
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
The Bee Census reached 55 respondents. Only 9 had ever paid, and some answers were gamed. This asks people who have paid instead.

- Adds the **Honey Census** issue form: why people first bought, what got in the way, who pays, how they use Pollinations now, price feel, plan preference, what would make them use it more and which other AI tools they pay for. Pick lists have an optional free-text box for other answers
- Adds a 10 Quest Pollen quest, payable only to accounts that have bought Pollen: a Stripe checkout, a paid auto top-up or a Polar order. The two written answers need 100 characters in total
- Pauses the Bee Census (`state: "completed"`): it leaves the board, and late answers still pay. Deleting that line reopens it
- Counts only visible characters in written answers. One response passed the 60-character minimum with invisible U+200E filler
- Skips `HONEY-CENSUS` issues in triage and on the project board

**Before merging:** create the `HONEY-CENSUS` label. An issue form applies only labels that already exist.

Tests: the quest suite passes (43/43), including the new purchase-gate and invisible-filler cases. Typecheck is clean.

gist.headline: A census for the honey jar
gist.blurb: The Bee Census makes room for the Honey Census, a survey for people who’ve bought Pollen. Eligible buyers can earn 10 Quest Pollen for answers with a little substance.
gist.summary: The Honey Census adds a survey about Pollen purchases and usage, plus a 10 Quest Pollen reward for buyers with a Stripe checkout, paid auto top-up, or Polar order; its two written answers must contain 100 visible characters in total.
gist.impact: Pollen buyers get a dedicated way to share what led them to buy and what would help them use Pollinations more, while the Bee Census leaves the quest board and still rewards late answers.
